signals.title: EUR/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Tension
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags JPY as the weekly leader at +1.098% across 7 pairs against EUR as the laggard at −0.678% across 9 pairs, generating a 1.776% leader-to-laggard divergence. EUR/JPY trades at 177.517 while testing negative BEER model valuation at z=−1.95σ. Middle East escalation headlines and Strait of Hormuz transit disruptions layer risk-off pressure on top of heavy EUR positioning, despite the ECB 2.65% vs BoJ 1.25% +140bp carry advantage favoring EUR. Options confirm pronounced downside hedging with EUR/JPY 25-delta risk reversals printing an extreme put skew of −2.42. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/JPY, downside momentum reinforced by geopolitical safe-haven flow. Catalyst: Germany Factory Orders release at 06:00 UTC. Risk: Strait of Hormuz de-escalation headline relieves geopolitical risk premia and forces short-covering.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning + Vol + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1256, positioned below its SMA20 at 1.1464, SMA50 at 1.1530, and SMA200 at 1.1613. CFTC data shows leveraged funds net short EUR at −82,445 contracts (week ending Sep 29) sitting at the 6th percentile (z=−1.65), while retail sentiment shows an extreme 87% long positioning on Retail sentiment data. This stark institutional short versus retail long divergence indicates severe retail trapped-long exposure. Implied volatility trades at 6.9% against 30-day realized volatility of 3.9%, generating an elevated vol risk premium of +3.1% alongside a 25-delta risk reversal put skew of −1.53. Fed policy rate of 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% maintains a +135bp carry advantage in favor of the dollar, while US 5Y yields rose +47bp over 20D (FRED, as of Oct 01) driven by real yields (+46bp real vs +1bp breakeven). Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, structural policy divergence and institutional flow dominate. Catalyst: Euro Area Composite PMI release at 08:00 UTC. Risk: Leveraged funds trigger short-covering above the SMA20 at 1.1464.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail Extreme + Policy Spread
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4254, holding above its SMA20 (1.4019), SMA50 (1.3960), and SMA200 (1.3854) cluster. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment displays an extreme 95% short positioning, heavily fading the bullish spot trend. Leveraged funds hold CAD net short at −72,519 contracts after a WoW reduction of −23,396 contracts, demonstrating that retail is positioned directly against both trend momentum and broader institutional positioning. Macro carry structurally anchors the move, with the Fed at 4.00% vs BoC at 2.25% offering a +175bp policy rate advantage in favor of USD. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, persistent carry divergence alongside contrarian retail short exposure. Catalyst: Canada Trade Balance and Ivey PMI releases at 12:30/14:00 UTC. Risk: WTI crude spikes sharply above $95/bbl on Hormuz disruption, driving CAD recovery.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium vs Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 157.78, holding above its SMA20 at 156.26 while remaining below its SMA50 at 158.02. A 275bp Fed-BoJ policy rate spread (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%) keeps carry structurally favorable toward USD while VIX remains contained at 15.3 (normal volatility). However, 25-delta risk reversals print an extreme downside put skew of −2.36, indicating substantial options demand hedging a downward decline. Cross-asset signals show MOVE at the 98th percentile of its trailing year versus VIX at the 15th percentile, reflecting elevated bond market interest rate volatility that has not yet fed into equity stress. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry support intact while holding below overhead resistance. Catalyst: Japan Services PMI at 00:30 UTC and 10Y JGB Auction at 03:35 UTC. Risk: Sustained break below SMA20 at 156.26 accompanied by equity risk-off escalation.
